must_know.headline: Trump lands in Shenzhen as Xi and Putin vow a multipolar order ahead of Thursday's three-way summit
must_know.summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, where Xi Jinping personally greeted him, according to the South China Morning Post. Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin had met earlier and pledged to push a multipolar world, and both criticised Western protectionism and sanctions. Trump, Xi and Putin are due to hold a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit on Thursday.
must_know.why_it_matters: Xi has put Trump and Putin in one room on Chinese soil after publicly aligning with Putin against Western sanctions, so any outcome will be read against that backdrop by US allies who are already uneasy about what Washington might concede. The measure was announced in Geneva.

reporting_varies.angle: Analysts expect few concrete outcomes from the Trump-Xi talks, with rivalry between the two powers unresolved.
Frames the meeting as Trump meeting an 'anti-U.S. axis' and says allies worry what he might give up to get a trilateral pact.

must_know.headline: Iran fires at Kuwait and Bahrain after US strikes missile site on Qeshm Island The measure was announced in Geneva.
must_know.summary: Iran said it targeted US drone and missile sites at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem base overnight, after US fighter jets struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Tuesday. Kuwait and Bahrain said they repelled the attacks. Reuters called it Iran's first attack on Kuwait since September. Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian attacks for a third time in a week.
must_know.why_it_matters: A US strike meant as a limited reply to attacks on a Bahrain radar drew a second Gulf host state into the exchange within hours, while Qatari-Iranian talks on narrowing gaps were under way; each round now gives both sides a fresh reason to answer in kind.

reporting_varies.angle: Stresses that the attacks show obstacles to diplomacy; cites a US official saying the Qeshm strike answered Iranian attacks on US personnel, while Iranian media said it caused no damage.
Quotes Bahrain accusing Tehran of a 'systematic hostile approach'.

must_know.headline: Ukraine collapses section of Crimean Bridge in missile and drone strike days before Putin meets Trump and Xi
must_know.summary: Ukraine destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge overnight, and its military says no vehicle can cross. The rail line is damaged but still standing, and Russia's transport ministry said some rail services resumed. Zelensky called it an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making, carried out in seven stages with drones and Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".
must_know.why_it_matters: The strike hits the road link Russia uses to move troops toward the front and lands just as Putin heads into a summit with the US and Chinese presidents, handing Kyiv a visible counterpoint to his hoped-for moment in the spotlight.

reporting_varies.angle: Reports a company's claim that European-made Ruta missiles were the only foreign weapons used in the strike.
Pairs the strike with Russian missile hits on two Kyiv bridges the same night, a crater on the Northern bridge and traffic disruption, framing it as a battle of the bridges.
Presents Zelensky's images of the damage as a show of strength before the Trump-Putin meeting.

must_know.headline: World court to rule Thursday on whether Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
must_know.summary: The International Court of Justice is due on Thursday to deliver its judgment in the case The Gambia filed against Myanmar on November 11, 2019. The Gambia alleges Myanmar broke the 1948 Genocide Convention through military "clearance operations" against the Rohingya that began in 2016 and escalated in August 2017. Myanmar denies genocide and says it was targeting a military uprising by insurgents. More than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees remain in Bangladesh, most in camps in Cox's Bazar.
must_know.why_it_matters: A genocide finding would also settle how the court judges "intent", and the US and Israel reportedly fear that precedent could be used later in a case over Gaza, which is why fears are growing of US sanctions on ICJ judges, as the US has already imposed on ICC judges. The measure was announced in Geneva.

reporting_varies.angle: Focuses on Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh hoping for recognition, while noting a ruling may do little to change their lives soon because Myanmar remains in civil war under the same military.
Focuses on the geopolitical stakes: fears of US sanctions on ICJ judges, including ad hoc judge Navi Pillay, and a precedent that could affect a future ruling on Israel in Gaza.
reporting_varies.bias: Geopolitical, critical of US pressure on the court

should_know.headline: Rubio says no imminent threat to Washington after CNN reports Iranian dirty-bomb plot
should_know.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is no imminent threat to Washington after a CNN report that Iran may plan a "dirty bomb" attack on the US capital. President Donald Trump said the US takes the possibility "very seriously" and warned Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if a threat exists. Tehran called the report "baseless" and said it was an attempt to manufacture legitimacy for continuing the war, now in its ninth month.

should_know.headline: Nvidia doubles revenue to over $115bn, faces SEC probe as Huang agrees to testify to Congress
should_know.summary: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of more than $115 billion, double a year earlier, in its first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The Wall Street Journal reported the company faces an SEC probe after his exit, and Huang has agreed to appear before US congressional committees in December. Board chair Harvey Jones said Nvidia does not intend to reinstate Huang and promised a fast CEO search, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim chief.

should_know.headline: Israel's Knesset elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana speaker, defeating Netanyahu's camp
should_know.summary: Israel's parliament on Tuesday elected Matan Kahana, a lawmaker from Gadi Eisenkot's party, as speaker. He comes from the camp opposed to caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The speaker can advance bills from Eisenkot's bloc, such as an investigation of the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack, and the bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu's contentious policies. Netanyahu's party has claimed the Oct. 27 election was "stolen" by Arab-led parties, after heavy losses.

should_know.headline: US official says Ukraine's deep strikes in Russia fail; German minister calls criticism 'stupid'
should_know.summary: Elbridge Colby, a US defence official, told a meeting of Ukraine's allies at NATO headquarters in Brussels that spectacular strikes far behind the front have not helped end the war or stop Russia's advance. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called it "quite stupid" to criticise attacks on military targets in Russia. NATO chief Mark Rutte backed Ukraine's right to hit logistics hubs, and diplomats linked Colby's remarks to Ukraine's latest attack on the Crimean bridge.

should_know.headline: Russia reportedly demands NATO pull troops and bases back to 1997 positions
should_know.summary: Russian negotiators in Abu Dhabi presented a document dated November 10 that calls for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases to where they stood in 1997, The New York Times reports, according to Deutsche Welle. It also reportedly demands an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine. Russia is not explicitly demanding that eastern members leave the alliance, only that NATO end its military presence there. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev and Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal rejected any Russian say in Europe's security order.

should_know.headline: US to end South Africa and Rwanda's AGOA trade access from Jan. 1, 2027
should_know.summary: The Trump administration announced on Nov. 2 that it plans to end South Africa's and Rwanda's eligibility for AGOA, the US duty-free trade programme for sub-Saharan Africa, from Jan. 1, 2027. President Trump had signed a bill on Sept. 2 extending AGOA through the end of 2028. An Al Jazeera opinion piece argues the move shows Africa must speed up its own economic integration. It says South Africa is the programme's largest beneficiary, and that losing access can bring tariffs of 15 to 20 percent on some products.

should_know.headline: Ethiopian troops push Tigrayan forces toward Eritrean border, raising fears of wider war
should_know.summary: Ethiopian forces have driven Tigrayan fighters toward the Eritrean border, and ACLED reports skirmishes at several sites. Ethiopian heavy artillery has reportedly hit dwellings near the Eritrean border town of Badme. Tigray-allied fighters launched an offensive on Sept. 23 aimed at toppling the government. Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties in October, and Ethiopia-Sudan relations have also worsened, according to Deutsche Welle.

should_know.headline: Turnout falls at French pay marches as strike take-up in state administration drops below 3%
should_know.summary: Public and private sector workers marched in Paris and other French cities on Tuesday to demand higher wages. The CGT union counted 500,000 marchers nationwide; police counted 146,000. Reuters described the marches as largely peaceful with falling turnout, though clashes between radical groups and police broke out at the end in Paris. Only 2.59% of state administration staff struck, against about 10% on Nov. 5, according to a partial Public Accounts Ministry estimate.

should_know.headline: SoftBank's Son says missing Anthropic investment was a 'mistake' as IPO nears
should_know.summary: SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son called not backing Anthropic a mistake, the Financial Times and Nikkei Asia reported. The Japanese group had already begun investing in rival OpenAI. Anthropic's IPO is due this week, and the Financial Times says it is set to redraw venture capital's power rankings. The New York Times says the prospectus reads like dystopian science fiction.

should_know.headline: NSA classified network goes down as US tech outages spread; officials deny cyberattack
should_know.summary: The NSA's classified internal network, NSANet, was disrupted on Tuesday. The agency said it had "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance" and that mission-critical capabilities stayed fully operational. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was "zero evidence" the week's outages involving Microsoft, banks, Apple and flights are linked, and that the US is "not under systemic attack". House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries asked the administration to explain itself to Congress, and Trump said of the outages, "It's fine."
